question: When Meta reports on July 29, will it guide full-year 2026 capex above $145B?

model.prompt_context:
Resolution criteria:
- "Yes": Wins if Meta's Q2 2026 earnings press release or earnings call on July 29, 2026, as published on Meta's official Investor Relations website (investor.atmeta.com), provides full-year 2026 capital expenditure (capex) guidance with a midpoint or stated figure strictly above $145 billion.
- "No": Wins if Meta's Q2 2026 earnings press release or earnings call on July 29, 2026, as published on Meta's official Investor Relations website (investor.atmeta.com), provides full-year 2026 capital expenditure (capex) guidance whose midpoint or stated figure is $145 billion or below, or if Meta provides no full-year 2026 capex guidance in those materials.

Clarifications:
- "Above $145B" means strictly greater than $145 billion. A guidance range (e.g., $140B–$150B) is evaluated by its midpoint; if the midpoint is exactly $145B it does not qualify as above.
- Capex guidance refers to capital expenditures as defined and labeled by Meta in its official earnings materials (typically "capital expenditures" or "purchases of property and equipment"). Guidance for a sub-period (e.g., only H2 2026) does not constitute full-year guidance.
- If Meta issues a correction or update to its July 29 guidance before the market's settlement time, the most recently published figure from investor.atmeta.com is used.
